definition: Tidewater Georgian, offered as the place to begin: a variant of Georgian Colonial American, the first style the corpus filled end to end, read whole in its dossier, with an example brief to compose a house from.
more: The example stops at the brief. Its house has no plan that places: the plan written for it is refused, because its placement breaks facts of its own house type, so no sheet or export of it is drawn and the plan step names the conflict instead.
basis: Editorial. Which style is offered as the guided example is the workbench's own choice for Phase 14, and no corpus file names one; what the style is, is the corpus's. README.md: "Georgian Colonial is filled end to end" as its depth-first proof, and "Tidewater Georgian is then written as a" short override of it, "each resolving the rest from the parent". The example brief is briefs/family-georgian.json, the one docs/compose.md runs first. Where the example stops, in its more: build/revise.py, the corrective loop, on a placement already refused when it starts: "refused -> refused on a lower key is accepted, which is the Tidewater plan's own case"; and build/typefacts.py, the refusal to draw: "a placement that breaks a hard fact of the type is REFUSED, not" drawn. The measurement, and the other ways the example could have been answered, are in the open question on the worked house, which a glossary basis may not quote.
